blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Strategic cost management in logistics means knowing which costs create value and which do not. Not all cost reduction is good. Cutting the wrong cost can slow deliveries, damage client relationships or create hidden risks that surface only later, when they are far more expensive to fix.

At Czarnikow, the logistics team analyses costs across the full supply chain: freight rates, port charges, warehousing, insurance and customs duties. They separate fixed costs from variable ones, and they benchmark against market rates to find real savings — not the illusory kind that simply migrates a cost somewhere less visible.

The best logistics managers think in terms of total cost of ownership, not merely the cheapest quoted option. A slightly higher freight rate with a reliable carrier can save far more than a cheap rate that comes bundled with delays and penalties. The discipline, in the end, lies in distinguishing a good cost from a bad one — and defending the good ones when the pressure to cut is at its height.

items.q: According to the text, why is cutting the wrong cost dangerous?
options: It reduces the number of available carriers
It can create hidden risks that surface later, when they are costlier to fix
items.why: "create hidden risks that surface only later, when they are far more expensive to fix."

items.q: What distinction do the best logistics managers rely on?
options: Total cost of ownership versus the cheapest quoted option
items.why: "think in terms of total cost of ownership, not merely the cheapest quoted option."

items.q: What does the text mean by savings of "the illusory kind"?
options: Savings that are too small to record
Savings that only appear on forecasts
Savings that competitors have already achieved
A cost that is not removed but merely moved somewhere less visible
items.why: Inferência: "not the illusory kind that simply migrates a cost somewhere less visible" — o custo não desaparece, só muda de lugar.

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: Some costs are worth defending under pressure
The cheapest quoted rate is the truest measure of value
Not every cost reduction improves the business
A reliable carrier can be worth a higher freight rate
items.why: Inferência: todo o texto argumenta contra confundir o menor preço com o menor custo real.

items.q: The final sentence suggests that defending good costs is hardest…
options: precisely when the pressure to cut is greatest
items.why: Inferência: "defending the good ones when the pressure to cut is at its height" implica que é aí que o desafio aparece.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Sophie na reunião de diretoria. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Let me be candid about this twelve per cent target before we vote on it. I understand where it comes from, and I'm not against the number in principle. What I'm against is the plan behind it, because the plan cuts almost exclusively into resilience.

Those buffer stocks and the second carrier we keep on standby — that redundancy is exactly what absorbed the port strike last winter. It never shows a return in a normal quarter, which is precisely why it looks like an easy line item to delete. But it is insurance, and you do not judge insurance by the years it sits unused.

If the board wants twelve per cent, I can find it — but I have to find it in process waste and unused capacity, not in the things that keep us standing when a shock lands. We must not confuse a lean operation with a fragile one.

So my proposal is this: give me a fortnight, and I'll come back with a target that separates the good costs from the bad. Cutting blindly to hit a headline figure is how you accumulate a risk you only notice once it's too late to price.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What is Sophie's actual objection to the twelve per cent target?
options: The board voted without consulting logistics
The plan behind it cuts almost exclusively into resilience
The savings should come from freight rates alone
The number itself is too high
items.why: "I'm not against the number in principle… What I'm against is the plan behind it, because the plan cuts almost exclusively into resilience."

items.q: Why does Sophie say the redundancy "looks like an easy line item to delete"?
options: Because it never shows a return in a normal quarter
Because it is the largest cost on the budget
Because the board has already approved cutting it
Because the carriers requested its removal
items.why: "It never shows a return in a normal quarter, which is precisely why it looks like an easy line item to delete."

items.q: Where does Sophie say she would find the twelve per cent instead?
options: In headcount across the supply chain
In buffer stocks and standby carriers
In process waste and unused capacity
items.why: "I have to find it in process waste and unused capacity, not in the things that keep us standing."

items.q: What does Sophie imply with "you do not judge insurance by the years it sits unused"?
options: Insurance policies should be renewed annually
The value of the buffer is in the shock it prevents, not in routine quarters
The port strike was an isolated event unlikely to recur
items.why: Inferência: redundância é seguro — seu valor aparece na crise, não no funcionamento normal.

items.q: How would you best describe Sophie's stance?
options: She endorses the goal but challenges the method, offering an alternative
She rejects the target and refuses to engage with it
She accepts the target uncritically to satisfy the board
She is indifferent to where the cuts land
items.why: Inferência: ela aceita a meta em princípio, contesta o caminho e propõe uma alternativa concreta em duas semanas.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Cutting blindly lets risk quietly accumulate until it surfaces." To accumulate means to…
items.why: Accumulate = acumular-se, ir se somando aos poucos.

items.q: "The buffer stock is a form of redundancy." In this context, redundancy means…
options: duplicated capacity kept as a backup
a job that has been eliminated
a repeated line in a contract
items.why: Redundancy aqui = redundância: capacidade extra mantida como reserva para casos de falha.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "When margins are healthy, ___ about cost discipline sets in, and waste creeps back."
items.why: Complacency = complacência: a acomodação que aparece quando tudo vai bem.

items.q: "We must distinguish process waste from unused capacity." To distinguish means to…
items.why: Distinguish = distinguir, separar uma coisa da outra. (São problemas diferentes, com soluções diferentes.)

items.q: Choose the correct term: "A single point of failure could trigger a ___ loss that dwarfs any saving."
items.why: Catastrophic = catastrófico: perda devastadora, de outra ordem de grandeza.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs de reuniões sobre custo e logística. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "Sophie pushed back on the twelve per cent target." To push back on means to…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, contestar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "The board will not sign off on the cuts until logistics reviews them." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "Trimming the buffer stock will barely move the needle on total cost." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer uma diferença perceptível.

items.q: "We agreed the savings plan but never followed through on the audit." They…
options: failed to carry it to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.

items.q: "Before we cut freight, let's drill down into where the real waste sits." To drill down into means to…
items.why: Drill down into = aprofundar, examinar em detalhe camada por camada.
